version.changelog: v1.4.13 安全加固版：全功能包命令白名单兜底、专属包补连接安全声明、重算 legacy lock 基线

llm.summary: This is a disclosed ARI-backed Amazon seller planning skill that uses an API key and can spend ARI credits only after quote and confirmation.

dimensions.detail: Bash access is used to run the bundled CLI, and network requests are constrained in code and documentation to https://ari.funewa.com with redirects blocked.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: No package install or dependency bootstrap was found; the included CLI uses Python standard-library code and user-invoked commands.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Instructions narrow the skill to one seller action-plan workflow and exclude ads, inventory, profit, and arbitrary prompts; the CLI also exposes an optional competitor ASIN argument, but the documented fixed flow does not direct its use.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The setup/configure flow stores an ARI API key in ~/.ari/config.json with 0600 permissions; this is disclosed and purpose-aligned, with no background service or cross-session agent modification found.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose, fixed audit/action workflow, Amazon ASIN inputs, ARI API use, review collection, profile checks, quotes, and report generation fit together coherently.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install this only if you are comfortable using ari.funewa.com for Amazon product/review analysis and storing an ARI API key locally. Review the returned quote before confirming any collection or analysis run, since confirmed operations can spend ARI credits; also note that the documentation and CLI are primarily Chinese-language.
llm.findings:
[LP1] expected: Remote account, billing, collection, and analysis requests were verified, but the artifacts disclose the ARI API key requirement, the official endpoint, billing/credit checks, quote-before-run behavior, and collection/analysis workflow.
[EA2] unexpected: The cited autoconfirm text appears in the changelog as removed historical capability; the inspected CLI requires --confirm for paid collection and operations run.
[SQP-3] expected: Most user-facing text is Chinese and links use /zh; that affects audience and usability, but the skill is presented as a Chinese Amazon seller workflow rather than hidden security behavior.
[SDI-2] expected: Account and credit balance checks support authorization and paid-operation quoting, and are documented by the check command; competitor ASIN support is present in the CLI but not used by the documented fixed single-ASIN flow.
[P9] unexpected: The whitespace padding locations were manually inspected and contained blank spacing between normal functions, with no hidden instructions or concealed code found.
[SDI-1] expected: The available setup, configure, check, collect, status, and operations commands match the documented basic and fixed workflow commands, and a runtime allowedCommands whitelist is present.
[AST7] expected: The dynamic getattr use is limited to a fixed local tuple of argument names for ASIN validation, not arbitrary attribute exposure or command execution.
